This outbreak ranks as the second-largest and second-deadliest on record, surpassed only by West Africa’s 2014–2016 epidemic, which infected over 28,600 and killed about 11,000. The transmission is driven by the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. - DR Congo's Ebola outbreak has surpassed 11,000 cases, with 5,387 deaths reported. Government data show 11,042 confirmed Ebola cases in the country, making it the largest and most deadly outbreak in DR Congo's history. Eight of the country's 26 provinces have been affected, and many deaths have occurred outside treatment centers, underscoring access and care challenges. By comparison, the West Africa outbreak of 2014–2016 remains the largest on record with about 28,600 cases and over 11,000 deaths. The ongoing outbreak in DR Congo is attributed to the Bundibugyo ebolavirus variant. There is currently no approved vaccine or specific treatment for this variant, highlighting the need for enhanced surveillance, containment, and supportive care.
